Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

host noun

who receives guests

also hostess, the host, be host, our host

classical

Hor. S. 1.5.71: sēdulus hospes
Cic. Div. 1.57: alterum ad caupōnem dēvertisse, ad hospitem alterum (Lewis & Short)

hospes, hospitis m.

noun, third declension; feminine hospita, hospitae

host (and also guest)

One who takes a friend or a stranger under his roof for nothing; an innkeeper, caupō, is paid (Lewis & Short). The same word is the guest, and host and guest together are hospes hospitī (Cic. Deiot. 8): the sentence shows which is meant. A hostess is hospita (Cic. Verr. 2.2.24), which can also be a woman guest.

Other words

  • dominus, dominī m. — host of a dinner (with or without convīviī, epulī)

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Vatin. 13; Liv. 23.8 (Lewis & Short)

    Generally master or owner; at a dinner, the man who gives it (Lewis & Short).

  • convīvātor, convīvātōris m. — the giver of a dinner party

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Hor. S. 2.8.73; Liv. 35.49.6 (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx rāra: Hor., Liv.)

  • hospita, hospitae f. — hostess

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Traupman 329

Examples

  • sēdulus hospes paene macrōs ārsit dum turdōs versat in ignī

    our attentive host nearly burnt down while turning lean thrushes over the fireHor. S. 1.5.71–72

  • cum dēfēcēre, quī modo hospes fuerat, mōnstrātor hospitiī et comes

    when the food has run out, the man who was host a moment ago becomes guide to another welcome, and companionTac. Germ. 21.2–3

  • hic est leō hospes hominis, hic est homō medicus leōnis

    this is the lion who was the man’s host, this is the man who was the lion’s doctorGell. 5.14.30

See also visitor, guest, receive, invite, guest room, landlord.
